title: ACCA AA - Audit and Assurance
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the ACCA AA syllabus study guide. Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: An audit engagement team is explaining to a new client why an audit provides reasonable rather than absolute assurance that the financial statements are free from material misstatement. Which factor best explains this limit?
options: Auditors use sampling, judgement and evidence that is persuasive rather than conclusive
Auditors guarantee that every error above one currency unit is detected
Auditors test every transaction recorded in the accounting system
Auditors are responsible for preparing the financial statements
items.explanation: Auditing standards describe reasonable assurance as a high but not absolute level because auditors form conclusions from sampling, professional judgement and persuasive rather than conclusive evidence, and inherent limitations such as concealment remain. Absolute assurance would require testing every item and is not achievable.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Audit Framework and Regulation

items.stem: During the planning meeting for a limited company audit the engagement partner clarifies the respective responsibilities of the directors and the auditor. Which statement correctly describes those responsibilities?
options: The auditor is responsible for the accounting records and the internal controls
The directors prepare the financial statements and the auditor forms an opinion on them
The auditor prepares the financial statements and the directors audit them
The directors and the auditor are jointly responsible for preparing the financial statements
items.explanation: Management, under the oversight of those charged with governance, is responsible for preparing the financial statements and maintaining internal control. The auditor's responsibility is to obtain evidence and express an opinion on those statements, not to prepare them or guarantee their accuracy.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Audit Framework and Regulation

items.stem: The audit manager owns a small but material number of shares in an audit client. Under the ACCA Code of Ethics and Conduct, which threat does the shareholding most directly create?
options: An intimidation threat to independence
A familiarity threat to independence
A self-interest threat to independence
An advocacy threat to independence
items.explanation: A financial interest in a client can influence the auditor's judgement because the auditor benefits personally from the client's performance, which is the definition of a self-interest threat. A material direct financial interest generally cannot be reduced to an acceptable level by safeguards and the auditor should be removed.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Audit Framework and Regulation

items.stem: A trainee asks which International Standard on Auditing sets out the overall objectives of the independent auditor and the conduct of an audit in accordance with ISAs. Which standard should the trainee be told?
options: ISA 315
ISA 700
ISA 570
ISA 200
items.explanation: ISA 200 states the overall objectives of the independent auditor and explains the nature and scope of an audit designed to enable the auditor to express an opinion. ISA 315 deals with risk assessment, ISA 700 with the audit report and ISA 570 with going concern.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Audit Framework and Regulation

items.stem: A client asks whether a review engagement provides the same level of assurance as an audit of the same financial statements. Which statement is correct?
options: A review provides limited assurance based mainly on enquiry and analytical procedures
A review provides absolute assurance because fewer errors are expected
A review provides the same reasonable assurance as a full audit
A review requires the auditor to test the controls over the accounting system
items.explanation: A review engagement gives limited, negative assurance, expressed as nothing having come to the auditor's attention, and is based primarily on enquiry and analytical procedures rather than the detailed testing of an audit. It therefore gives less assurance than an audit.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Audit Framework and Regulation

items.stem: A candidate is asked who normally appoints the external auditor of a public company under typical company law. Which party is correct?
options: The external auditor's own firm
The shareholders in general meeting
The finance director of the company
The internal audit committee acting alone
items.explanation: While the board or audit committee may recommend a firm, company law generally vests the appointment of the external auditor in the shareholders in general meeting, and the auditor reports to the shareholders. This preserves auditor independence from executive management.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Audit Framework and Regulation

items.stem: An audit senior is asked by a friend who works at another company for details of an audit client's trading results before they are published. Which fundamental ethical principle is most directly implicated?
options: Objectivity
Professional competence and due care
Confidentiality
Professional behaviour
items.explanation: The principle of confidentiality requires an auditor not to disclose client information obtained in the course of professional work without authority, unless there is a legal or professional right or duty to disclose. Sharing unpublished results with a friend breaches that duty.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Audit Framework and Regulation

items.stem: Under ISA 300 an engagement team is establishing the overall audit strategy for a new assignment. Which activity belongs to this stage of the engagement?
options: Issuing the final independent auditor's report
Performing the detailed substantive testing of receivables
Obtaining the written representations from management
Determining the characteristics of the engagement that define its scope
items.explanation: ISA 300 requires the auditor to establish an overall audit strategy that sets the scope, timing and direction of the audit and guides development of the audit plan. Detailed substantive testing and written representations come later, and the report is issued at the end.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Audit Framework and Regulation

items.stem: During planning the auditor considers materiality for the financial statements as a whole. Which statement best defines materiality for the engagement?
options: Misstatements are material if they could reasonably influence the economic decisions of users taken on the basis of the financial statements
Materiality is any misstatement larger than one currency unit
Materiality is the total value of the company's assets
Materiality is set by the tax authority for the reporting period
items.explanation: ISA 320 defines materiality by reference to whether omissions or misstatements could reasonably be expected to influence the economic decisions of users. It is a matter of professional judgement and is not a fixed currency amount or a tax threshold.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Planning and Risk Assessment

items.stem: An audit partner explains why the team sets performance materiality at an amount lower than materiality for the financial statements as a whole. Which reason is correct?
options: To satisfy the directors that the accounts will be unqualified
To reduce to an appropriately low level the probability that the aggregate of uncorrected and undetected misstatements exceeds overall materiality
To increase the audit fee that will be charged to the client
To guarantee that no misstatement exists in the financial statements
items.explanation: ISA 320 requires performance materiality to be set lower than overall materiality so that the cumulative effect of individually immaterial misstatements, together with undetected ones, is unlikely to exceed overall materiality. It is a margin for aggregation and detection risk, not a fee or guarantee.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Planning and Risk Assessment

items.stem: A jewellery retailer holds stock that is small, high value and easily stolen. Which component of the audit risk model is most directly increased by this fact?
options: Control risk
Sampling risk
Inherent risk
Detection risk
items.explanation: Inherent risk is the susceptibility of an assertion to misstatement before consideration of controls, and it is raised by factors such as a high-value, portable inventory susceptible to theft. Control risk depends on the client's controls, and detection risk is a function of the auditor's own procedures.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Planning and Risk Assessment

items.stem: A trainee is revising the audit risk model before an exam. Which equation correctly expresses the relationship between the components of risk?
options: Audit risk equals inherent risk plus detection risk
Audit risk equals control risk divided by detection risk
Audit risk equals detection risk minus inherent risk
Audit risk equals inherent risk times control risk times detection risk
items.explanation: The model expresses audit risk as the product of inherent risk, control risk and detection risk. Because detection risk is the only component the auditor controls directly, a higher assessment of inherent or control risk requires a lower acceptable detection risk and therefore more testing.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Planning and Risk Assessment

items.stem: Under ISA 240 a newly qualified auditor explains the firm's responsibility in relation to fraud in an audit of financial statements. Which statement is correct?
options: To obtain reasonable assurance that the financial statements are free from material misstatement whether caused by fraud or error
To detect all fraud regardless of whether it is material
To prevent fraud by designing the client's internal controls
To guarantee that employees never commit fraud
items.explanation: ISA 240 makes the auditor responsible for obtaining reasonable assurance that the statements are free of material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error, and for maintaining professional scepticism. Management, not the auditor, has primary responsibility for preventing and detecting fraud.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Planning and Risk Assessment

items.stem: An auditor receives a management explanation that conflicts with other evidence obtained during the audit. How should the auditor respond?
options: Reduce the extent of testing because the explanation saves time
Apply professional scepticism and obtain further appropriate audit evidence before accepting the explanation
Accept the explanation because management is presumed to be honest
Withdraw from the engagement immediately in every case
items.explanation: Professional scepticism requires the auditor to question contradictory evidence and not to accept management's representations without corroboration. The auditor should investigate and obtain further evidence rather than accept the explanation or reduce testing.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Planning and Risk Assessment

items.stem: ISA 315 requires the auditor to understand the entity and its environment. Which item would the auditor most likely identify as a business risk affecting the audit?
options: The company has recruited a new office cleaner
The board has changed the meeting room used for meetings
A major customer accounting for most of the entity's revenue has entered administration
The colour of the company's logo has recently changed
items.explanation: A significant customer failure threatens going concern and revenue recognition and therefore affects the risk of material misstatement. Trivial operational changes such as cleaners or meeting rooms have no bearing on the audit, and a logo change is a marketing matter.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Planning and Risk Assessment

items.stem: An audit team plans analytical procedures at the planning stage of the engagement. What is the main purpose of these procedures at that point?
options: To prove that the financial statements are correct
To replace all substantive testing at the year end
To calculate the audit fee payable by the client
To identify unusual relationships that may indicate higher risks of material misstatement
items.explanation: At the planning stage analytical procedures are a risk assessment tool used to highlight unusual or unexpected relationships and direct attention to areas of higher risk. They do not prove accounts are correct, cannot replace all substantive testing, and are unrelated to the fee.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Planning and Risk Assessment

items.stem: A listed company has both substantial profit before tax and substantial revenue. Which benchmark might the auditor typically consider when setting overall materiality?
options: A percentage of profit before tax or of revenue depending on what is most relevant to users
Always the number of employees in the entity
Always the amount of cash held at the year end
The amount of the management bonus pool
items.explanation: ISA 320 paragraph A3 suggests benchmarks such as profit before tax, total revenue, gross profit or total equity, and the auditor chooses the one most relevant to users' decisions. Employee numbers, year-end cash or a management bonus pool are not appropriate benchmarks.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Planning and Risk Assessment

items.stem: The auditor assesses the risk of material misstatement for the valuation assertion on inventory. Which basis is this assessment most closely tied to?
options: The number of audit partners in the firm
The assertion level, because risks are assessed for classes of transactions, account balances and disclosures
The engagement letter only
The auditor's fee estimate
items.explanation: ISA 315 requires the risk of material misstatement to be assessed at the assertion level for classes of transactions, account balances and disclosures so that further procedures can be designed to address each assertion. The engagement letter, fee and firm size are not assertions.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Planning and Risk Assessment

items.stem: A sales manager's bonus depends entirely on reported sales growth. Which fraud risk factor does this represent?
options: An ethical control that prevents fraudulent reporting
A confirmation from the bank that cash exists
An incentive or pressure that may motivate fraudulent financial reporting
A lack of internal control over cash receipts
items.explanation: The fraud triangle comprises incentive or pressure, opportunity and rationalisation. A bonus tied to reported growth pressures management to manipulate revenue, which is an incentive factor, whereas opportunity arises from weak controls.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Planning and Risk Assessment

items.stem: Before accepting a new audit engagement the firm should agree the terms of the engagement in writing with management. What is the main purpose of the engagement letter?
options: To guarantee that the audit opinion will be unmodified
To transfer the directors' responsibility for the accounts to the auditor
To set the audit fee at a fixed percentage of profit
To reduce the risk of misunderstanding about the respective responsibilities of management and the auditor
items.explanation: The engagement letter documents the agreed terms, including the scope, the responsibilities of management and the auditor, and the expected form of report, in order to avoid misunderstandings. It cannot guarantee an opinion and does not transfer directors' legal responsibilities.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Planning and Risk Assessment

items.stem: A prospective audit client has a history of questionable business practices and refuses to allow access to certain records. What should the firm consider before accepting the engagement?
options: Whether the integrity of the client and the firm's ability to obtain sufficient evidence make acceptance appropriate
Nothing, because all fees are welcome
Only whether the client is able to pay the fee
Whether the firm can ignore the missing records and still issue an opinion
items.explanation: ISA 220 and ethical requirements make the firm consider client integrity, independence and its ability to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence before acceptance, and to decline if these cannot be satisfied. Fee matters alone are not a proper basis for acceptance.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Planning and Risk Assessment

items.stem: During the audit the auditor becomes aware of a matter that would have changed the materiality level set at planning. What should the auditor do?
options: Automatically issue a modified audit opinion
Revise materiality and consider whether it is necessary to revise the nature, timing and extent of further audit procedures
Ignore the matter because materiality was already approved by the partner
Complete the audit without any change to the planned procedures
items.explanation: ISA 320 requires the auditor to revise materiality and to reconsider the nature, timing and extent of further procedures if the auditor becomes aware of information that would have caused a different materiality to be set initially. It does not automatically lead to a modified opinion.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Planning and Risk Assessment

items.stem: Under ISA 315 a trainee is listing the components of the entity's system of internal control. Which of the following is one of those components?
options: The independent auditor's report
The auditor's own quality control file
The control environment
The engagement acceptance checklist
items.explanation: ISA 315 identifies five components of the system of internal control, being the control environment, the entity's risk assessment process, the information system and communication, control activities, and monitoring of controls. The other options are engagement or firm documents, not components.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Internal Control

items.stem: An auditor is distinguishing the control environment from control activities. Which factor is part of the entity's control environment rather than a control activity?
options: A three-way matching of purchase order, goods received note and invoice
A bank reconciliation prepared monthly by a ledger clerk
A password policy applied to the payroll system
The commitment of those charged with governance to integrity and ethical values
items.explanation: The control environment is the tone set by those charged with governance and management, including integrity, ethical values and governance. Matching documents, preparing a reconciliation and enforcing a password policy are specific control activities.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Internal Control

items.stem: Why does the auditor perform tests of controls when the risk assessment expects the client's controls to operate effectively?
options: To obtain evidence that the controls operated effectively throughout the period and support a reduced level of substantive testing
To replace all substantive procedures without exception
To evaluate the competence of the finance director
To confirm the audit fee for the following year
items.explanation: Tests of controls evaluate the operating effectiveness of controls and, if effective, allow the auditor to assess control risk lower and reduce substantive testing. They do not eliminate the need for all substantive work, and they do not assess individuals or fees.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Internal Control

items.stem: In a small company one employee is responsible for both ordering goods and approving the related payment. Which control weakness does this create?
options: A reliable detective control over inventory
A lack of segregation of duties that increases the risk of misappropriation
A strengthening of the control environment
An effective preventive control over receipts
items.explanation: Segregation of duties requires that no single person should be able to both perpetrate and conceal an error or fraud. Combining ordering and payment approval in one person removes that check and raises the risk of misappropriation. The other options wrongly describe the arrangement as effective.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Internal Control

items.stem: An auditor is classifying controls over a computerised accounting system. Which item is an example of an IT general control rather than an application control?
options: A limit on the credit available to a customer
A validation that a date field is in the correct format
Controls over program changes and access to the accounting system
A check that a sales order cannot be invoiced twice
items.explanation: IT general controls support the reliable operation of the IT environment as a whole, such as program change management, access security and backup. Duplicate invoice checks, credit limits and field validation operate inside a specific application and are therefore application controls.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Internal Control

items.stem: A monthly bank reconciliation is designed to find errors after they have occurred. Which type of control is it?
options: A preventive control
A corrective control that stops the error at entry
An inherent risk
A detective control
items.explanation: A detective control is designed to identify errors or irregularities after they have occurred, and a bank reconciliation identifies discrepancies between the cash book and the bank statement. Preventive controls aim to stop errors from arising, and inherent risk is not a control at all.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Internal Control

items.stem: An auditor identifies a significant deficiency in internal control during the audit. To which party should the deficiency be communicated?
options: In writing to those charged with governance
Only to the audit junior who found it
To the tax authority as a formal report
To no one because deficiencies are never reported
items.explanation: ISA 265 requires the auditor to communicate significant deficiencies in internal control in writing to those charged with governance on a timely basis. They are not reported to the tax authority and cannot simply be ignored, although they are generally not included in the audit report on the accounts.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Internal Control

items.stem: For a small owner-managed entity where the auditor cannot rely on internal controls, which approach is most appropriate?
options: An approach that tests only the owner's approval signature
A substantive approach using tests of detail and analytical procedures
A purely controls-based approach relying on segregation of duties
No audit procedures because the entity is small
items.explanation: Where segregation of duties is limited and controls cannot be relied upon, the auditor should adopt a substantive approach, obtaining evidence from tests of detail and substantive analytical procedures. The other options either misapply a controls approach or omit the audit work required.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Internal Control

items.stem: The auditor assesses control risk as high for the revenue cycle. What is the effect of that assessment on the audit approach?
options: No further audit work is needed in the revenue cycle
The audit opinion automatically becomes adverse
More extensive substantive procedures are required because detection risk is set lower
Less substantive testing is required because control risk is high
items.explanation: If control risk is assessed as high, the auditor cannot rely on controls and must set detection risk lower, which requires more extensive and effective substantive procedures. High control risk does not reduce testing, and it does not automatically change the opinion.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Internal Control

items.stem: An audit team performs a walkthrough of a significant class of transactions. What is the main purpose of this procedure?
options: To provide conclusive proof that the accounts are correct
To test the mathematics of every invoice in the population
To satisfy a legal requirement to visit the client's premises
To confirm the understanding of the process and that controls have been implemented
items.explanation: A walkthrough traces one or a few transactions through the system to confirm the auditor's understanding of the process and that the identified controls have been implemented. It is not a test of the whole population and does not by itself provide sufficient evidence that accounts are correct.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Internal Control

items.stem: A payroll system rejects an employee record that omits the national insurance number. Which type of application control is this?
options: An input validation or completeness check control
An IT general control over program changes
A physical access control to the server room
A reconciliation between the payroll and the general ledger
items.explanation: Rejecting a record because a required field is missing is an input validation control, often described as a completeness or mandatory field check, applied within the payroll application. IT general controls, physical access and reconciliations are different controls with different objectives.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Internal Control

items.stem: Management reviews monthly exception reports comparing budget to actual results and investigates large variances. Which component of internal control does this illustrate?
options: Information processing controls only
Monitoring of controls
The control environment
The entity's risk assessment process
items.explanation: Monitoring of controls is the process of assessing the quality and effectiveness of internal control over time, and management review of exception and variance reports is an example. The control environment concerns tone and governance, while risk assessment identifies and analyses risks.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Internal Control

items.stem: Which statement best describes the requirement for audit evidence that an auditor must satisfy under ISA 500?
options: Evidence is sufficient if it can be obtained cheaply
Only oral evidence from the finance director is required
The auditor must obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence to reduce audit risk to an acceptably low level
The auditor must obtain all evidence that exists in the entity
items.explanation: ISA 500 requires sufficient (quantity) and appropriate (relevance and reliability) evidence to reduce audit risk to an acceptably low level. Gaining all evidence is impossible, cost alone is not a basis, and oral evidence from management is generally the least reliable form.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Audit Evidence and Procedures

items.stem: An auditor is ranking the reliability of different forms of evidence gathered on an engagement. Which form is generally considered the most reliable?
options: Written representations from the client's management
A verbal explanation from the client's ledger clerk
A draft schedule prepared by an employee of the client
Evidence obtained directly by the auditor from an independent external source
items.explanation: ISA 500 states that evidence is more reliable when obtained from independent external sources and when it is documentary rather than oral. Management representations and internal schedules are client-generated and therefore less reliable, and verbal evidence is least reliable.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Audit Evidence and Procedures

items.stem: An auditor wants to obtain evidence about the existence of year-end trade receivables. Which procedure is most appropriate?
options: Sending external confirmation requests directly to the customers
Asking the sales ledger clerk to list the balances from memory
Reviewing the prior year's receivables aging schedule only
Recalculating the depreciation of delivery vehicles
items.explanation: External confirmation, a form of third-party direct evidence, is well suited to testing the existence of receivables balances and their valuation when combined with other procedures. Client listings, prior-year schedules and vehicle depreciation do not address the receivables assertion.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Audit Evidence and Procedures

items.stem: The auditor selects a sample of goods received notes and traces them to the purchase ledger to ensure they are recorded. Which assertion is being tested?
options: Valuation of purchases
Completeness of purchases
Existence of purchases
Rights and obligations of purchases
items.explanation: Tracing from source documents to the accounting records tests whether transactions that occurred have been recorded, which addresses the completeness assertion. Testing existence would instead trace from the ledger back to the source documents.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Audit Evidence and Procedures

items.stem: The auditor selects entries in the sales ledger and agrees them back to dispatch notes and customer orders. Which assertion is being tested?
options: Cut-off of revenue
Classification of revenue
Occurrence of revenue
Completeness of revenue
items.explanation: Testing from the ledger back to underlying documents establishes whether recorded sales actually occurred, which addresses the occurrence assertion. Tracing in the opposite direction, from documents to the ledger, would test completeness.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Audit Evidence and Procedures

items.stem: The auditor draws a sample and the conclusion differs from the conclusion that would be reached by testing the whole population. What is this called?
options: Non-sampling risk
Inherent risk
Control risk
Sampling risk
items.explanation: Sampling risk is the risk that the auditor's conclusion based on a sample may differ from the conclusion reached if the entire population were tested. Non-sampling risk arises from reasons unrelated to sampling, such as an inappropriate procedure or a failure to recognise an error.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Audit Evidence and Procedures

items.stem: The auditor examines the shipping log and the sales ledger either side of the year end to ensure sales are recorded in the correct period. Which assertion is being tested?
options: Cut-off
Rights and obligations
Classification
Understandability
items.explanation: Cut-off testing checks that transactions and events are recorded in the correct accounting period, an aspect of the occurrence and completeness assertions for revenue. It examines items around the year end rather than the entity's legal rights or the presentation of the accounts.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Audit Evidence and Procedures

items.stem: The auditor is unable to attend the client's inventory count at an off-site warehouse. What should the auditor consider first?
options: Relying solely on the prior year's count sheet
Performing alternative procedures or arranging attendance at a count near the reporting date
Accepting management's statement that the count was accurate
Ignoring the inventory because it is held off-site
items.explanation: When the auditor cannot attend the count, ISA 501 requires alternative procedures such as attending another count or inspecting the inventory, or obtaining evidence about the count by other means. Simply accepting management's word or the prior-year sheet would not provide sufficient appropriate evidence.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Audit Evidence and Procedures

items.stem: Which procedure provides the most reliable evidence about the existence of the cash at bank balance in the financial statements?
options: The cash book maintained by the client
An oral statement from the finance director
A direct bank confirmation letter obtained from the bank
A schedule of cash balances prepared by the client's finance team
items.explanation: A bank confirmation provides direct, third-party documentary evidence of the balance, which is more reliable than client-maintained records. The cash book and internal schedules are produced by the client, and an oral statement is the least reliable form of evidence.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Audit Evidence and Procedures

items.stem: The auditor compares the current year's payroll cost with the prior year, adjusting for known pay rises and headcount changes. Which type of procedure is this?
options: A test of the client's control environment
An external confirmation
A physical inspection of assets
A substantive analytical procedure
items.explanation: Substantive analytical procedures evaluate financial information by studying plausible relationships among data, such as payroll cost against headcount and pay rates. The other options describe different evidence-gathering techniques rather than analysis of relationships.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Audit Evidence and Procedures

items.stem: After the year end but before the auditor signs the report, a customer with a large balance at the year end is declared bankrupt, confirming a receivable that was overstated. How should this event be treated?
options: As an adjusting event that provides evidence of a condition existing at the year end
As a non-adjusting event requiring disclosure only
As an event that is ignored because it happened after the year end
As a reason to change the year-end date of the financial statements
items.explanation: ISA 560 distinguishes adjusting events, which provide evidence of conditions that existed at the year end and should be reflected in the amounts recognised, from non-adjusting events that arose afterwards. The bankruptcy confirms the receivable was impaired at the reporting date.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Review and Reporting

items.stem: After the reporting date the company's factory is destroyed by fire. The factory existed and was operating at the year end. Which treatment is correct?
options: A reason to restate the prior year's opening balances
A non-adjusting event, with disclosure if material, because it does not relate to a condition at the reporting date
An adjusting event reducing the carrying value of the factory at the year end
An event that must be ignored completely with no disclosure
items.explanation: The fire arose after the reporting date and does not provide evidence of a condition existing at that date, so it is a non-adjusting event. Under IAS 10 it should be disclosed if material, but the factory should not be written down in the year-end accounts themselves.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Review and Reporting

items.stem: Under ISA 570 a newly promoted manager explains the auditor's responsibility in relation to going concern. Which statement is correct?
options: To prepare the cash flow forecasts used to support the going concern assessment
To ignore going concern unless the client specifically asks about it
To obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence about the appropriateness of management's use of the going concern basis
To guarantee that the entity will continue in operation for at least ten years
items.explanation: ISA 570 requires the auditor to evaluate management's assessment of the entity's ability to continue as a going concern and to conclude whether a material uncertainty exists. The auditor does not guarantee survival, does not prepare the forecasts, and must always consider going concern.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Review and Reporting

items.stem: The auditor concludes that the financial statements contain a material misstatement and management refuses to correct it. Which opinion is most appropriate?
options: An unmodified opinion with no further action
A disclaimer of opinion in all cases
No opinion is issued and the matter is left to the directors
A qualified or adverse opinion depending on whether the misstatement is material or pervasive
items.explanation: Under ISA 705 a material but not pervasive misstatement results in a qualified opinion, while a material and pervasive misstatement results in an adverse opinion. An unmodified opinion would be wrong, and a disclaimer is used when the auditor cannot obtain evidence, not when there is a known misstatement.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Review and Reporting

items.stem: The auditor wants to draw attention to a matter that is appropriately presented in the financial statements without modifying the opinion. Which approach is used?
options: Include an Emphasis of Matter paragraph in the audit report
Issue an adverse opinion on the financial statements
Issue a disclaimer of opinion on the financial statements
Remove the matter from the financial statements
items.explanation: An Emphasis of Matter paragraph draws users' attention to a matter that is appropriately presented or disclosed in the financial statements and does not modify the opinion. An adverse opinion or disclaimer indicates that the opinion itself is modified, and the auditor cannot remove items from the accounts.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Review and Reporting

items.stem: Which engagement is most likely to require an engagement quality control review under ISQM 2?
options: An internal file review performed by the audit junior
An audit of the financial statements of a listed entity
A small compilation of management accounts for a sole trader
A bookkeeping engagement for a dormant company
items.explanation: ISQM 2 requires an engagement quality review for audits of financial statements of listed entities and for other engagements where required by law or where the firm determines it is appropriate. Smaller non-audit engagements and internal file reviews by assistants do not meet that requirement.
items.reference: ACCA AA Syllabus Study Guide - Review and Reporting
